name: semver
tagline: The library npm uses to read, compare and match version numbers like 1.2.3 and ranges like ^1.2.0.

source.note: semver v7.7.3, unchanged except one line in ranges/subset.js (line 233, in higherGT: the two operators swapped) so that real tests fail.

districts.name: Classes
districts.summary: The three core types: SemVer (one version), Comparator (one condition like >=1.2.0) and Range (a whole range made of comparators).

districts.name: Functions
districts.summary: Small helpers that work on single versions: parse, clean, compare, sort, bump with inc, and diff, which names the kind of change between two versions.

districts.name: Internal
districts.summary: Plumbing shared by everything else: the big regular expressions, constants and limits, option parsing, a tiny cache and debug logging.

districts.name: Ranges
districts.summary: Helpers that work on ranges: is a version inside or outside a range, the lowest or highest match, and whether two ranges overlap.

const parseComparator = (comp, options) => {
  comp = comp.replace(re[t.BUILD], '')
  debug('comp', comp, options)
  comp = replaceCarets(comp, options)
  debug('caret', comp)
  comp = replaceTildes(comp, options)
  debug('tildes', comp)
  comp = replaceXRanges(comp, options)
  debug('xrange', comp)
  comp = replaceStars(comp, options)
  debug('stars', comp)
  return comp
}

const replaceTildes = (comp, options) => {
  return comp
    .trim()
    .split(/\s+/)
    .map((c) => replaceTilde(c, options))
    .join(' ')
}

functions.name: outside
functions.code:
const outside = (version, range, hilo, options) => {
  version = new SemVer(version, options)
  range = new Range(range, options)

  let gtfn, ltefn, ltfn, comp, ecomp
  switch (hilo) {
    case '>':
      gtfn = gt
      ltefn = lte
      ltfn = lt
      comp = '>'
      ecomp = '>='
      break
    case '<':
      gtfn = lt
      ltefn = gte

fix.explanation: When two lower bounds share a version, higherGT must keep >X over >=X because it is stricter. The bug swapped the operators, so it kept >=X and subset gave wrong answers.

guide.intro: This is semver, the code npm uses to understand version numbers. Each building is a file, each floor a function. One building is on fire: a real test is failing.
guide.onFire: subset.js is burning, in higherGT. 3 checks fail: it now thinks >2.0.0 is looser than >=2.0.0, so subset answers wrongly for ranges with the same lower version.
guide.done: All 8,827 checks pass again. Two operators in higherGT went back to their places and the fire is out.
